Annualized core operating return on tangible equity (ROTE) was 21.6% and annualized core operating ROE was 14.9%. ● Book value and tangible book value per share increased 5.1% and 5.7%, respectively, from September 30, 2025. Tangible book value per share excluding AOCI was up 15.4% over the same period. ZURICH – October 20, 2026 – Chubb Limited (NYSE: CB) today reported net income for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 of $2.84 billion, or $7.30 per share, and core operating income of $2.98 billion, or $7.66 per share. Book value per share and tangible book value per share increased by 5.1% and 5.7%, respectively, from September 30, 2025 and now stand at $191.43 and $126.96. For the last three months, book value was unfavorably impacted by after-tax net realized and unrealized losses of $4.48 billion in Chubb’s investment portfolio, partially offset by $551 million of foreign currency gains. Book value per share and tangible book value per share excluding AOCI increased by 11.1% and 15.4% from September 30, 2025. Effective Q3 2026, segment income and core operating income have been redefined to exclude intangible amortization expenses related to purchased intangibles other than long-term distribution agreements. Refer to “Regulation G – Non-GAAP Financial Measures” in this press release and the Table of Contents page in the Q3 2026 Chubb Limited Financial Supplement for additional information. Prior-period results have been restated to reflect these changes. Evan G. Greenberg, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Chubb Limited, commented: “We had a really strong quarter with strong contributions from all of our businesses. Our diversification is highly supportive of growth and sustained margins which speak to our underwriting discipline, a hallmark of our company. “P&C underwriting, investment and life income results led to core operating earnings of $2.98 billion, or $7.66 per share. Due to particularly light CAT losses last year, earnings are down 2% and up 1% per share from 2025. For the first nine months of the year, which is a more meaningful perspective, core operating income is a record $8.6 billion, or $21.94 per share, up 21% and 24.5%, respectively, from the prior year. “Annualized core operating return on tangible equity is 21.6% and core operating ROE is 14.9%. Tangible book value per share is up 5.7% from the prior year. This was impacted by the mark-to-market due to higher interest rates. Adjusting for AOCI, tangible book value per share increased 15.4%. “For the quarter, P&C underwriting income is $2.1 billion, which led to a combined ratio of 84.1%, and on a current accident year ex-CAT basis, our combined ratio is 82.6%, simply excellent. Year-to-date underwriting income of $5.8 billion is up nearly 34% from 2025. Chubb ® , Chubb logo ® and Chubb. Insured. SM are trademarks of Chubb. 3 Chubb Limited News Release “On the investment side of our business, adjusted net investment income is a record $1.9 billion, supported by rising interest rates and an excellent fixed-income investment environment, which we have been anticipating for some time, given government deficits and the capital investment cycle. On the alternative asset side, as publicly announced in the quarter, Strategic Holdings, our holding company partnership with KKR, agreed to sell our investment in USI Insurance Services to Aon, which is expected to result in a realized gain of $460 million on an investment of $740 million. “While the market continues to grow more competitive in commercial P&C across the board, particularly in the U.S. and London, the substantial majority of our underwriting businesses grew in the quarter, with the balance flat or purposely shrinking due to inadequate pricing or terms. “We are benefiting from our diversification. Overseas General grew 6.7%, with Latin America up 11.7%, Asia up 7.5% and Europe up about 7%. North America personal lines was up 5.3% and agriculture was up 5.1%. North America commercial was down 2.7%, impacted by a reduction in exposure, including increased use of reinsurance and underwriting related non-renewal actions, predominantly property and financial lines-related. I fully expect North America commercial growth to improve in future quarters. “Our deep local presence and capabilities globally, our large and growing invested asset along with rising interest rates, and operating discipline provide us continued growth opportunities and sustainability of value creation. I am confident in our ability to continue to outperform and to generate strong growth in operating earnings and EPS and, most important, double-digit growth in tangible book value.” Chubb ® , Chubb logo ® and Chubb. reference.summary: Chubb Limited provides insurance and reinsurance products worldwide. It operates in six segments: North America Commercial Property and Casualty (P&C) Insurance, North America Personal P&C Insurance, North America Agricultural Insurance, Overseas General Insurance, Global Reinsurance, and Life Insurance. The company offers property and general liability, workers' compensation, and umbrella; professional and management liability; environmental, health, and international coverages; and claims and risk management products and services, loss control, and engineering and complex claims management. It also provides homeowners, automobile and collector cars, valuable articles, and personal and excess liability insurance.
